figure.alt: Coordinate plane with a solid line through (0, 5) and (10, 0); the region on and below the line is shaded.

questions.prompt: The shaded region shown represents the solutions to which inequality?
questions.explanation: The boundary line passes through \((0, 5)\) and \((10, 0)\). Its slope is \(m = \frac{0 - 5}{10 - 0} = -\frac{1}{2}\), and its \(y\)-intercept is \((0, 5)\), so \(b = 5\). The boundary line is \(y = -\frac{1}{2}x + 5\). The shaded region is the set of points on and below this line, so it represents \(y \le -\frac{1}{2}x + 5\). Choice A is incorrect: its boundary line has a \(y\)-intercept of \((0, -5)\), not \((0, 5)\) (sign error). Choice C is incorrect: its boundary line has a \(y\)-intercept of \((0, 10)\); the value 10 comes from the \(x\)-intercept, not the \(y\)-intercept. Choice D is incorrect: its boundary line has a \(y\)-intercept of \((0, -10)\); the value 10 comes from the \(x\)-intercept, not the \(y\)-intercept.

questions.source: Variant of Practice Test 2 · Module 1 · Q11
questions.prompt: In triangle \(RST\), \(RS = 3{,}850\) yards (yd) and \(ST = 3{,}850\) yd. Which statement is sufficient to prove that triangle \(RST\) is equilateral?
questions.explanation: A triangle is equilateral when all three sides have the same length. Since \(RS = ST = 3{,}850\) yd, the triangle is equilateral exactly when \(RT = 3{,}850\) yd as well. The other choices are 3,850 yd divided by a power of 10 (a place-value slip), so they would make \(RT\) shorter than the other two sides, and the triangle would not be equilateral.

questions.source: Variant of Practice Test 2 · Module 1 · Q12
questions.prompt:
\(V(t) = 18.5(0.93)^t\)

The function \(V\) gives the predicted value, in thousands of dollars, of a used car \(t\) years after it was purchased, for \(0 \le t \le 10\). According to the model, what is the best interpretation of the statement “\(V(5)\) is approximately equal to 12.87”?
choices: When the car was purchased, its predicted value was approximately 5 thousand dollars.
12.87 years after the car was purchased, its predicted value was approximately 5 thousand dollars.
5 years after the car was purchased, its predicted value was approximately 12.87 thousand dollars.
When the car was purchased, its predicted value was approximately 12.87 thousand dollars.
questions.explanation: \(V(5)\) is the value of \(V(t)\) when \(t = 5\). The input \(t\) is the number of years since the car was purchased and the output is its predicted value in thousands of dollars, so “\(V(5) \approx 12.87\)” means that 5 years after the car was purchased, its predicted value was about 12.87 thousand dollars ($12,870). Choices A and D describe the time of purchase (\(t = 0\)), when the model gives \(V(0) = 18.5\) thousand dollars. Choice B swaps the input and the output.

questions.source: Variant of Practice Test 2 · Module 1 · Q12
questions.prompt:
\(N(w) = 1{,}200(1.08)^w\)

The function \(N\) gives the predicted number of trout in a lake \(w\) weeks after the lake was stocked, for \(0 \le w \le 20\). According to the model, what is the best interpretation of the statement “\(N(9)\) is approximately equal to 2,399”?
choices: When the lake was stocked, the predicted number of trout in the lake was approximately 2,399.
2,399 weeks after the lake was stocked, the predicted number of trout in the lake was approximately 9.
When the lake was stocked, the predicted number of trout in the lake was approximately 9.
9 weeks after the lake was stocked, the predicted number of trout in the lake was approximately 2,399.
questions.explanation: \(N(9)\) is the value of \(N(w)\) when \(w = 9\). The input \(w\) is the number of weeks since the lake was stocked and the output is the predicted number of trout, so “\(N(9) \approx 2{,}399\)” means that 9 weeks after the lake was stocked, the predicted number of trout was about 2,399. Choices A and C describe the moment of stocking (\(w = 0\)), when the model gives \(N(0) = 1{,}200\) trout. Choice B swaps the input and the output.

\(P(a) = 101.3(0.88)^a\)

The function \(P\) gives the predicted air pressure, in kilopascals, at an altitude of \(a\) kilometers above sea level, for \(0 \le a \le 8\). According to the model, what is the best interpretation of the statement “\(P(3)\) is approximately equal to 69.03”?
choices: At sea level, the predicted air pressure is approximately 3 kilopascals.
At an altitude of 3 kilometers above sea level, the predicted air pressure is approximately 69.03 kilopascals.
At sea level, the predicted air pressure is approximately 69.03 kilopascals.
At an altitude of 69.03 kilometers above sea level, the predicted air pressure is approximately 3 kilopascals.
questions.explanation: \(P(3)\) is the value of \(P(a)\) when \(a = 3\). The input \(a\) is the altitude in kilometers above sea level and the output is the predicted air pressure in kilopascals, so “\(P(3) \approx 69.03\)” means that at an altitude of 3 kilometers, the predicted air pressure is about 69.03 kilopascals. Choices A and C describe sea level (\(a = 0\)), where the model gives \(P(0) = 101.3\) kilopascals. Choice D swaps the input and the output.

questions.source: Variant of Practice Test 2 · Module 1 · Q13
questions.prompt: A soup can is shaped like a right circular cylinder. The can has a volume of 425 cubic centimeters, and the area of its base is 25 square centimeters. What is the height, in centimeters, of the can?
questions.explanation: The volume of a right circular cylinder is \(V = \pi r^2 h\), where \(\pi r^2\) is the area of the circular base. Substituting \(V = 425\) and \(\pi r^2 = 25\) gives \(425 = 25h\). Dividing both sides by 25 gives \(h = 17\). The height is 17 centimeters.

questions.source: Variant of Practice Test 2 · Module 1 · Q14
questions.prompt:
The list gives the mass, in grams, of 5 rabbits.

2,040; 2,040; 1,560; 2,080; 1,530

What is the mean mass, in grams, of these 5 rabbits?
questions.explanation: The mean is the sum of the values divided by the number of values. The sum is \(2{,}040 + 2{,}040 + 1{,}560 + 2{,}080 + 1{,}530 = 9{,}250\). There are 5 values, so the mean is \(\frac{9{,}250}{5} = 1{,}850\) grams.

questions.source: Variant of Practice Test 2 · Module 1 · Q15
questions.prompt:
\(x = 7\)
\(y = (10 - x)^2\)

A solution to the given system of equations is \((x, y)\). What is the value of \(xy\)?
questions.explanation: Substitute \(x = 7\) into the second equation: \(y = (10 - 7)^2 = (3)^2 = 9\). Then \(xy = (7)(9) = 63\). Choice A is \(x + y\) instead of \(xy\). Choice B is \(7(10 - 7)\), which forgets to square. Choice D comes from computing \((10 + 7)^2 = 289\) instead of \((10 - 7)^2\).

questions.prompt: What is the value of \(\cos S\) in the triangle shown?
questions.explanation: The cosine of an acute angle in a right triangle is the length of the leg adjacent to the angle divided by the length of the hypotenuse. In the triangle shown, the leg adjacent to angle \(S\) has length 15 and the hypotenuse (the side opposite the right angle) has length 17. So \(\cos S = \frac{15}{17}\). questions.source: Variant of Practice Test 2 · Module 1 · Q17
questions.prompt: A circle has a radius of 19 millimeters. What is the area, in square millimeters, of the circle?
questions.explanation: The area of a circle is \(A = \pi r^2\). Substituting \(r = 19\) gives \(A = \pi(19)^2 = 361\pi\) square millimeters. Choice A uses the diameter, 38, in place of the radius: \(\pi(38)^2 = 1{,}444\pi\). Choice C is the circumference, \(2\pi r\). Choice D is \(\pi r\), which forgets to square the radius.

questions.source: Variant of Practice Test 2 · Module 1 · Q17
questions.prompt: A circular trampoline has a radius of 7 feet. What is the area, in square feet, of the trampoline?
questions.explanation: The area of a circle is \(A = \pi r^2\). Substituting \(r = 7\) gives \(A = \pi(7)^2 = 49\pi\) square feet. Choice B is the circumference, \(2\pi r\). Choice C is \(\pi r\), which forgets to square the radius. Choice D is \(\frac{\pi r}{2}\).

Choice B is the circumference, \(2\pi r\). Choice D uses the diameter, 62, in place of the radius: \(\pi(62)^2 = 3{,}844\pi\).

questions.source: Variant of Practice Test 2 · Module 1 · Q18
questions.prompt: A gold nugget has a mass of 57.9 grams and a volume of 3 cubic centimeters. What is the density, in grams per cubic centimeter, of the nugget?
questions.explanation: Density is mass divided by volume. The density is \(\frac{57.9\text{ grams}}{3\text{ cubic centimeters}} = 19.3\) grams per cubic centimeter. Choice A is \(57.9 \times 3\), which multiplies instead of divides. Choice B is \(57.9 + 3\) and choice C is \(57.9 - 3\).

questions.source: Variant of Practice Test 2 · Module 1 · Q18
questions.prompt: A granite paving stone has a mass of 540 grams and a volume of 200 cubic centimeters. What is the density, in grams per cubic centimeter, of the stone?
questions.explanation: Density is mass divided by volume. The density is \(\frac{540\text{ grams}}{200\text{ cubic centimeters}} = 2.7\) grams per cubic centimeter. Choice A is volume divided by mass, \(\frac{200}{540} = \frac{10}{27}\), which is upside down. Choice C is \(540 - 200\) and choice D is \(540 + 200\).

Choice B is volume divided by mass, \(\frac{200}{184} = \frac{25}{23}\), which is upside down. Choice C is \(200 - 184\) and choice D is \(184 + 200\).
